transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-05 10:00 PDT
- Duration: ~57 minutes
- Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Rajiv, Ayesha, Lena, Tom (Blue Oak)

Summary:
Quick sync focused on last week's POC results: structured output failures when invoking tool-calls from SDK, intermittent invalid JSON returns, and how the Redwood SDK and runtime handle fallback/latency when kv cache / batching kicks in. Customer emphasized regulatory requirements (audit logs, KMS) for production. Agreed next steps: share repro, run failure harness, schedule security checklist review.

Topics:
- SDK function-calling failure modes
- Structured-output schema validation and linting
- Observability: token-level traces, audit logs, mismatch between model and app contract
- Private/VPC/KMS constraints and timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie: okay good morning everyone thanks for carving out time, uh quick check in on the POC, we have about 45 minutes ish which should be fine, um, Ethan will kick off with the repro notes.
[00:14] Ethan: yeah hi all, thanks, so last week we saw three main failure patterns when Blue Oak calls function/tool endpoints through the SDK — one was truncated structured output, two was schema mismatch where the model returned an array instead of object, and three was a latency-induced partial streaming that left the json invalid.
[00:34] Ayesha: yeah we hit the array thing a lot, like sometimes it will return ["action1","action2"] instead of {"actions": [...]}, and our downstream consumer blew up, so we had to add defensive parsing which is ugly.
[00:48] Lena: from SRE perspective the intermittent invalid JSONs correlate with request spikes and when the kayvee cache — kv cache? — is warming, so maybe it's a pipeline buffer flush issue but we also see some 5xxs from the Redwood endpoint during batching changes.
[01:12] Ethan: right, and to be precise, the runtime does continuous batching; when the batch gets truncated mid-stream due to a timeout we can end up with incomplete chunks. There's an option to enforce per-request flushing or to adjust the streaming chunk size. We suggested toggling the SDK's streaming chunk param in the sandbox.
[01:36] Rajiv: are those toggles available on Hosted or do they require Dedicated / Private? We need to know if we can tune this before committing to Reserved capacity.
[01:46] Sophie: good question. Most streaming toggles are available on Hosted API. However, for strict SLOs and deterministic latency we'd recommend Dedicated — that gives you reserved GPU pools and more control over batching policies. For Private deployments you get the same controls but with VPC configs and your KMS.
[02:03] Tom: quick procurement question — if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commitment? we are still evaluating costs.
[02:09] Sophie: the AE side will follow up with details in an email; for the POC we're not changing your billing, still covered under the trial. We'll send a pricing sheet after this call.
[02:22] Ayesha: back to failures — Ethan you mentioned per-request flushing, can you show the SDK snippet? last week the one you sent had the "call_function" wrapper but our service stubs didn't handle the error codes consistently.
[02:36] Ethan: yeah I'll paste a snippet after the call, but core idea is to set 'streaming_chunk_ms' to a lower value and enable 'strict_schema_validation' in the SDK middleware. Note: current SDK versions prior to 0.9.4 have a bug where the middleware swallow certain parsing errors — we've got a patch branch.
[02:59] Ayesha: oh we are on 0.9.2 — okay that explains it, we hit that bug.
[03:05] Sophie: action item, Sophie will share the patched SDK build + minimal repro.
[03:12] Maya: also, for structured output we recommended using the SDK's schema linter which can be run as a pre-commit check. Ethan, can you add rules for arrays vs objects and required fields?
[03:25] Ethan: yes, I'll create example linter config and a simple node/python snippet. We'll include an example of failing and passing responses so your CI can reject bad outputs.
[03:36] Lena: question about observability: we saw mismatches between the tokens reported in the app and the token breakdown in the Redwood console, is that expected?
[03:47] Ethan: sometimes the console aggregates tokens at the route level and rounding differences plus streaming truncation can make small deltas. For token-level diffs, we can enable debug tracing which tags each request with a trace id and you can correlate traces with logs. Note that enabling debug tracing increases log volume.
[04:09] Rajiv: for compliance, we need audit logs for every inference and KV cache hits/misses retained for 90 days, also encryption in transit and at rest with our KMS. Can Redwood support HSM-backed keys?
[04:24] Sophie: yes, Private has KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; Hosted has configurable retention but HSM is part of Private offering. We'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, integration docs).
[04:38] Tom: procurement follow-up — can you include SLAs around uptime and latency in the doc? we want a target p50/p95 numbers for our SLA evaluation.
[04:49] Sophie: we'll include typical metrics and dedicated SLA options.
[04:54] Ayesha: one weird behavior — when we enabled the SDK's caching layer the model sometimes returns stale tool-call outputs, like it repeats a previous function response. Is that expected?
[05:06] Ethan: the SDK's prefix caching stores token prefixes to reduce cost; if your prompt shape often includes identical prefixes the cache may return hits. For action/tool calls we recommend configuring the cache to bypass for things flagged as non-idempotent. There's an option 'cache_scope'=("request","session","prefix") — try setting to session or disable for tool endpoints.
[05:33] Ayesha: okay, yeah that might explain it — we left default to prefix. We'll flip to session for the tool calls.
[05:39] Lena: also when we tested offline replay harness we saw the model sometimes emit different schemas for the same prompt across seeds, how do we lock output shape?
[05:52] Ethan: two levers: 1) structured-output schema enforcement in the SDK which rejects outputs not matching the JSON schema, and 2) model variant pinning plus sampling params (temperature=0, top_p low) to reduce variability. Combined they give deterministic shape but you might still need post-validate + fallback.
[06:16] Rajiv: does Redwood Optimize recommend quantized variants for this workload? we are heavy on inference-per-dollar and a lot of small short queries.
[06:26] Sophie: yes Optimize can recommend quantization and batching levels. For short queries, smaller model variants with aggressive quantization often win on cost without latency impact. We'll share a report after you run the workload profile.
[06:38] Ayesha: timeline wise we need to present to execs next month, so preferably a hardened sandbox with schema linter and deterministic responses.
[06:47] Sophie: understood — target ship of hardened sandbox + repro by Aug 12 so you can run validation before the exec deck.
[06:56] Ethan: one more technical note: function-calling signature mismatches can be mitigated by adding a small wrapper that normalizes model output before handing off to downstream services; we can provide that wrapper in the SDK examples.
[07:12] Rajiv: are there known competitors who provide stronger built-in schema enforcement? we evaluated a few.
[07:18] Sophie: some vendors like Anthropic and OpenAI have tools, but Redwood focuses on runtime + SDK integration — the advantage is you get both kernel-level batching control and app-level schema enforcement together.
[07:33] Tom: procurement note — include a section on data residency and EU-only hosting (we have EU users).
[07:41] Sophie: will do. We'll include region options.
[07:45] Ayesha: last thing — can you add a check for function call retries? we saw double-invocations when the client retried on timeout.
[07:55] Ethan: yes, we recommend idempotency tokens on tool calls and the SDK now supports automatic dedupe for calls with id tokens, but it's opt-in. We'll add an example.
[08:07] Maya: Okay let's recap next steps briefly.
[08:10] Sophie: recap: 1) Sophie shares patched SDK + repro, 2) Ethan shares schema linter + linter rules + wrapper examples, 3) Ayesha runs failure-harness and shares logs, 4) Lena sends SSO metadata and security constraints, 5) schedule security checklist with Redwood security (week of Aug 17).
[08:32] Rajiv: fine. thanks everyone.
[08:36] Tom: thanks, bye.
[08:38] (call ends)
